newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-CHILAVERT SAYS HE WILL PLAY DESPITE BAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHILAVERT SAYS HE WILL PLAY DESPITE BAN.

text.p: Paraguay captain Jose Luis Chilavert said on Friday his lawyers had appealed against a 13-month ban he received for fighting and he would play for his Argentine club Velez Sarsfield on Sunday.

A judge on Thursday banned the Paraguayan goalkeeper from professional soccer in Argentina for punching a stadium assistant on the head in a game between Velez Sarsfield and Gimnasia y Esgrima de la Plata in April 1994.
The player also received a three-month suspended jail sentence for the incident, which triggered a near-riot.
But Chilavert told reporters on Friday he would be out on the pitch for the next match. "On Sunday I just have to think about beating Independiente," he said.
The 31-year-old goalkeeper repeated allegations that the press persecuted him and said his lawyers had appealed against the ruling.

Chilavert, a Paraguayan national hero who scored from a free-kick against Argentina to clinch a draw in a World Cup qualifying match in Buenos Aires last Sunday, said he was being victimised because of his nationality.
"They can't forgive me my success because I'm Paraguayan but I feel more proud of that than ever," he said.
He said he trusted his lawyers would solve the problem but added that, if they did not, he might seek a club in another country.
Chilavert's case has attracted the attention of world soccer's governing body FIFA, which said on Friday in Zurich it would investigate the case.
FIFA has always argued that disciplinary action should be taking by sporting bodies, not law courts.
"Apart from anything else, he's from Paraguay and is playing in Argentina which makes it an international issue," a FIFA spokesman said.

Julio Grondona, head of the Argentine Football Association, said that as far as he was concerned, Chilavert could play: "We haven't received any official notification of the ruling from the courts," he said.
Paraguay's ambassador told Argentine radio the court's decision seemed "strange" but that he was confident Chilavert would eventually be cleared.
Ambassador Gustavo Diaz de Vivar said he would give the player legal assistance if necessary. But he played down Chilavert's accusations of discrimination against Paraguayans.
"Hundreds of thousands of Paraguayans live here and they get on marvellously with the Argentines," he said.
Chilavert, a menacing figure in goal who wears a bulldog design on his chest, says he wants to become president of Paraguay one day and impose his own brand of law and order.
